title: Tell Him the Actual Thing
scripture_text: In nothing be anxious, but in everything, by prayer and petition with thanksgiving, let your requests be made known to God. And the peace of God, which surpasses all understanding, will guard your hearts and your thoughts in Christ Jesus.
body:
Paul wrote this from a prison cell, which is worth knowing before you decide he was being glib.

"Let your requests be made known to God" is a plainer instruction than we usually treat it. Not your tidied-up requests. Not the version you would be comfortable praying out loud in a group. The actual thing — the audition, the diagnosis, the friendship that has gone quiet, the sin you have not said out loud to anyone.

God already knows it. The telling is not for His information. It is for you: naming a fear to God is how it stops being a shapeless weight and becomes a specific thing that a specific Person is now holding with you.

Notice what Paul promises and what he does not. He does not promise you will get what you asked for. He promises peace that guards you — a garrison word, a soldier posted at the gate of your thinking. The circumstances may not move. The thing standing between you and panic will.

So be specific today. Vague prayers are hard to see answered.
discussion_questions: What is the one thing you have not actually told God about?
Why is thanksgiving in the same sentence as anxiety here?
What would peace 'guarding your thoughts' look like in your week?
activity: Write down three specific requests and one thing you are thankful for. Keep the page — come back to it in a month.
